big_idea: Detectives ASK questions of the data and write a CONCLUSION. The data tells the story.
learning_intention: We are learning to ask and answer questions about data and write a conclusion.
student_learning_goal: I can ask and answer questions about a data display and write a conclusion.
success_criteria: I can ask 2 questions about a pictograph.
I can answer my questions using the data.
I can write ONE conclusion sentence.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dot and Tally puppets — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
All previous manipulatives at 5 capstone phases
Lesson 5 capstone rubric — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Detective Dot: I have a class survey. ASK me a question. I'll answer with the DATA.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dot + Tally puppets in detective hats. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL 5 detective steps: ASK, SORT, TALLY, GRAPH, CONCLUDE.'

Review each step quickly:
1. ASK a question. ('Which fruit is favourite?')
2. SORT or COLLECT. (Survey classmates.)
3. TALLY. (Count answers with 4+1.)
4. GRAPH. (Build a pictograph with title and labels.)
5. CONCLUDE. (Write a sentence about what the data shows.)

Introduce vocabulary. Write CONCLUSION on chart. 'Conclusion = what the data tells us — a sentence we WRITE.'

Demo. Show a pre-built pictograph: 'Class Pets — 6 dogs, 4 cats, 2 fish.' Ask 2 questions:
- 'Which is the GREATEST?' (Dogs.)
- 'How many MORE dogs than fish?' (4 more.)

Write a CONCLUSION: 'Most children in our class have dogs. Fish are the least common pet.'

More conclusion examples:
- 'More children like apples than bananas.'
- 'The greatest number of children chose hockey.'
- 'There are FEWER children with fish than with cats.'

'Detective Dot says — every case ENDS with a conclusion. The data tells the story; YOU write it.'

'Today YOU run a detective case from start to finish.'
student_actions: Watch Detective Dot solve the case.

steps.instruction: Each child gets a Detective Case Template. The class works through all 5 steps individually with teacher pacing.
Step 1-2 (5 min): Ask + Survey. Child picks a question card or invents one. Surveys 5-8 classmates.
Step 3-4 (10 min): Tally + Graph. Child draws tally marks AND builds a pictograph on the template.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Tally. Then graph with one-to-one. Add title and labels.'

steps.instruction: Step 5 (5 min): Conclude. Child writes ONE conclusion sentence. Teacher offers 'most / least / more than / fewer than' frames.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'What does your data tell us? Write your conclusion.'

steps.instruction: Circulate to record summative evidence on the capstone rubric.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Ask 'Show me your conclusion.' Mark the rubric.

differentiation.for_emerging: Pre-printed question + 3-classmate survey only. Sentence frame for conclusion.
differentiation.for_extending: Survey 10 classmates. Write 2 conclusion sentences with 'most', 'least', and a comparison.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a fill-in-the-blank conclusion: 'Most children chose ___. The least chosen was ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk around the room to survey, physically gather data, then sit to graph and conclude.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: asks question; tallies; graphs with one-to-one; orders by frequency; writes conclusion.

discussion_prompts: How does the DATA tell the story?
What was your favourite detective step?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child shares ONE conclusion: 'My data shows that ___.'

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Detective case template with question, tally, pictograph, ordering, and conclusion.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures D1.5 (analysis + conclusion) and reinforces D1.1-D1.4 in one integrated case.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child writes 'I like apples' as a conclusion — repairing the personal-not-data conclusion at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on D1.5 is the personal-not-data conclusion: the child writes a sentence about THEIR own preference instead of what the DATA shows about the GROUP. They miss that conclusions are about the data, not the writer.

This matters because data analysis requires looking at the WHOLE GROUP, not just oneself.

The walkthrough covers when a child writes a personal conclusion.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone session. Child has surveyed 8 classmates: 5 picked apples, 2 picked bananas, 1 picked grapes. Their conclusion reads 'I like apples.' Teacher reads it.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You like apples — that's true! But the conclusion has to be about the DATA. Look — what did MOST children pick?'

Walk through. 'Count: 5 picked apples. 2 picked bananas. 1 picked grapes. The GREATEST is APPLES at 5. So a data conclusion says: MOST children in our class chose apples.'

Generalise. 'Detective Dot says — write about the GROUP, not yourself. Use words like MOST, LEAST, MORE THAN, FEWER THAN.'

Now help the child rewrite. 'Try: "Most children chose apples. The fewest chose grapes."'

If still personal: provide a sentence-frame strip. 'Most children chose ___. Fewer chose ___.' Force the group framing.

Long-term recovery: every conclusion uses group language.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Writes group conclusion with sentence frame.
(Strong) Writes a clear group conclusion using 'most' or 'least'.
(Stretched) Writes a comparison conclusion ('more children chose apples than bananas').
common_misconceptions: Conclusion = my opinion. (Repair: conclusion = what the GROUP'S data shows.)
Conclusion is the answer to my favourite. (Repair: it's the answer to the question 'what does the data say?')
One sentence isn't a conclusion. (Repair: ONE sentence using 'most' / 'least' is enough at G1.)
recovery_moves: Read conclusions aloud and check against the data.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Summative artifact applying D1.1-D1.5 in one detective case.

parts_outline.task: Pick a question and survey 5 classmates. Draw tally marks.
Build a pictograph from your tally. Add title and labels.
Write ONE conclusion sentence about your data.
